title: Half-timber, stained glass and a red sign
label: Brand gallery
lede: One freely licensed photograph of a closed restaurant, one of the sibling chain, and three captures of the brand’s own website. The drawings are our own and do not reproduce the chain’s logo or crest.

archive.caption: A closed Steak and Ale at Westminster Mall, Colorado, May 13, 2011. The photographer notes it was demolished between July 2011 and March 2012.
archive.alt: An empty single-story restaurant with white walls, dark timbering and a brick chimney, with a red sign on a pole at the edge of a bare parking lot

archive.caption: A Bennigan’s in Denver, Colorado, from the John Margolies Roadside America archive at the Library of Congress.
archive.alt: A Bennigan’s restaurant with green awnings beside a parking lot
archive.credit: Photo: John Margolies, via [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Bennigan%27s_Restaurant,_Denver,_Colorado_LCCN2017709086.tif), Public domain.

archive.caption: The chain’s home page on February 3, 2003.
archive.alt: A blue web page with a Steak and Ale Restaurant logo and round photo buttons for locations, menu and banquets
archive.credit: Internet Archive capture of steakandale.com. Shown for commentary.

archive.caption: The chain’s last home page design, captured on January 5, 2008.
archive.alt: A beige web page with a sepia photograph of a dining room and buttons for locations, Steak 101 and banquets
archive.credit: Internet Archive capture of steakandale.com. Shown for commentary.
